title: Argent external device provider, contract version 1
description: A provider descriptor written to `~/.argent/providers/<any-name>.json`, listing the provider's identity and the devices it is currently offering. See `packages/device-providers/src/contract.ts` for the zod schemas these definitions mirror; `packages/device-providers/test/schema-parity.test.ts` fails the build if the two drift.

providerId.description: Unique per LIVE provider instance. Shape it as <vendor>-<instance>: Argent reports only the leading <vendor> segment in telemetry and treats the rest as opaque.

nativeId.description: The real iOS UDID or adb serial. Constrained because it reaches xcrun/adb as argv: no leading '-' and no shell or whitespace characters.

httpUrl.description: A page for a person to open. Never fetched by Argent.

simulatorServerUrl.description: An endpoint on the provider's own simulator-server. http:// only: the binary serves plaintext on a local port it picks at startup, and Argent opens /ws on the same host, so the WebSocket has to know its scheme up front.

capability.description: A mechanism the provider grants. Argent ignores tokens it does not recognise, so a provider may declare capabilities from a newer Argent version.

schemaVersion.description: Any other value and Argent skips this provider silently. That is the guarantee that a provider can never break Argent.

name.description: Human-readable. Shown to the agent and in every error attributed to this provider.

supportUrl.description: Where Argent points users when something fails on this provider's device. Strongly recommended: without it, the provider's bugs land in Argent's tracker.

pid.description: The process that wrote this file. Argent's runtime ignores it entirely; its only job is to let tooling (`argent providers prune`) remove descriptors left behind by a provider that died without withdrawing. Omit it and a crashed instance's descriptor has to be removed by hand.

workspace.description: Optional project context, surfaced verbatim in list-devices so an agent can prefer the device belonging to the project it is working in. Argent does no filtering of its own.

devices.description: The devices on offer right now. Required — an empty array is the correct way to say 'I am running but have nothing booted', and is meaningfully different from omitting the field (which is malformed). Republish whenever a device starts or stops.

providerDevice.title: One device a provider is offering

platform.description: Must agree with what nativeId's shape implies, or Argent rejects the device — classification stays single-sourced.

state.description: Free text in the platform's own vocabulary (e.g. 'Booted', 'device').

capabilities.description: REQUIRED. A device without this field is rejected: absent must never read as 'allow everything'.

simulatorServer.description: Required when the 'simulator-server' capability is declared. Argent probes apiUrl during discovery as its liveness signal — a device whose server is not listening is dropped from list-devices.

version.description: Informational. Argent never branches on it, but surfaces it in errors so version skew is diagnosable.

deviceSet.description: iOS only. The CoreSimulator device set the simulator lives in; present means Argent scopes every simctl verb with --set <deviceSet>. Absent means the default set.

metroPort.description: The Metro port serving this device. Supplies the default port for every tool that speaks CDP to the app's JS runtime, so a caller never has to be told where the bundler is; an explicitly requested port still wins. Independent of the 'js-debugger' capability, which decides whether argent may attach at all.

jsDebugger.description: Where to attach a CDP client instead of the target Metro advertises. React Native's inspector-proxy admits exactly one debugger per device and evicts the incumbent to accept a new one, so a provider that is already debugging this runtime should re-serve its own connection here and multiplex it. Omit it when nothing else is debugging, and argent connects to Metro directly. Argent still reads Metro for the session's metadata; only the socket changes.

webSocketUrl.description: ws:// or wss:// URL speaking the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

nativeDevtools.description: Where to attach to the native-devtools agent already inside the app, instead of injecting Argent's own dylib. DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES and the agent's endpoint are simulator-wide launchd values, so two products arming their own injection overwrite each other, and two builds of the same agent in one process would duplicate its classes and swizzles. A provider that already injects should re-serve its agent connection here and stay the only one in the app. The socket speaks the same newline-delimited JSON envelope Argent's own agent does — { type: 'Control' | 'ViewInspector' | 'CDP', payload } — opening with a Control frame naming the connected bundleId.

socketPath.description: Path to a listening unix socket. Bounded by sockaddr_un.sun_path, which is 104 bytes on macOS.
